object_context: Initial analytic-lane obstruction for BSD over Q: for an elliptic curve E/Q with ord_{s=1} L(E,s)=2, identify an unconditional, source-bound arithmetic bridge that can certify two independent Mordell-Weil directions and support the rank-two regulator/Sha part of the refined BSD formula, without assuming BSD itself, an equivalent main conjecture, or a rank-one theorem outside its hypotheses.
structural_coordinates: the official Clay/Wiles rank statement is ord_{s=1} L(E,s)=rank E(Q) for elliptic curves over Q
the refined leading coefficient contains the Tate-Shafarevich order, a rank-by-rank Neron-Tate regulator determinant, real period, bad-prime local/Tamagawa factors, and torsion denominator
analytic rank two forces even functional-equation sign and L(E,1)=L'(E,1)=0 with L''(E,1) nonzero after normalization
Gross-Zagier is intrinsically a first-derivative/height-of-Heegner-point bridge in its classical rank-one setting
Kolyvagin-style Euler-system arguments turn suitable nontrivial classes into strong Selmer bounds but their classical Heegner-point success is rank-one scoped
rank two requires independence, not merely existence: a single non-torsion point proves only rank at least one
a rank-two arithmetic certificate naturally has determinantal/exterior-power structure and must survive the passage from Selmer information to actual Mordell-Weil rank
finiteness and exact size of Sha are logically separate from rank equality and are needed for the full leading-term formula
p-adic or anticyclotomic control does not automatically identify the complex second derivative or the global leading coefficient
current accepted status remains unsolved; unreviewed 2026 claims cannot be imported as theorem authority
equivalent_formulations: for analytic-rank-two E/Q, produce two Z-independent rational points and prove there are no further independent points
prove Selmer corank two together with enough control of Sha to identify Mordell-Weil rank two
construct a nonzero rank-two exterior/determinantal arithmetic class and prove that its nonvanishing is forced by the analytic second-order zero
establish a rank-two height/regulator identity that connects L''(E,1) to the determinant of a Neron-Tate pairing on two independent global points
close the rank-two piece of the refined BSD leading-term formula with exact local factors, torsion, period, regulator, and Sha normalization
solved_analogues: analytic-rank-zero and analytic-rank-one BSD rank equality for elliptic curves over Q, via modularity together with Gross-Zagier/Kolyvagin-type results as summarized in the official Clay/Wiles problem description
near_solved_analogues: higher-rank Euler/Kolyvagin/Stark-system formalism of Burns-Sano, which supplies exterior-power algebraic machinery under explicit representation and Selmer hypotheses

Chan-Ho Kim's higher Gross-Zagier/Selmer-structure preprint, which treats arbitrary-rank Selmer structures but explicitly separates nontriviality/main-conjecture inputs from a number-field higher-rank analytic formula

method_transfers.source_context: Gross-Zagier plus Kolyvagin in the analytic-rank-one regime
method_transfers.method: first obtain a source-bound arithmetic witness from central L-function behavior, then use an Euler/Kolyvagin system to turn witness nontriviality into an upper bound on the relevant Selmer group
shared_structure: central L-function vanishing order is to be related to global arithmetic rank
height pairings encode non-torsion arithmetic information
Selmer groups mediate between cohomological classes and Mordell-Weil/Sha information
required_assumptions: the exact modular/Heegner and local hypotheses of the invoked rank-one results
nontriviality of the relevant Heegner/Kolyvagin classes
correct passage from Selmer bounds to Mordell-Weil rank and Sha finiteness
disanalogies: analytic rank two has even sign and the classical first derivative vanishes, so the classical one-point Gross-Zagier witness is not a two-dimensional certificate
one non-torsion point or one rank-one Kolyvagin class cannot certify two independent Mordell-Weil directions
the refined rank-two formula requires a 2x2 regulator determinant and additional Sha/local-factor control
method_transfers.repair_question: What rank-two exterior or determinant-level arithmetic object can replace the single Heegner-point witness, and what unconditional analytic statement forces its nonvanishing when ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=2?
source_anchors: Gross-Zagier, Heegner points and derivatives of L-series, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), DOI 10.1007/BF01388809
Kolyvagin, Finiteness of E(Q) and Sha(E,Q) for a subclass of Weil curves, Math. USSR-Izv. 32 (1989), DOI 10.1070/IM1989v032n03ABEH000779

method_transfers.source_context: Burns-Sano higher-rank Euler, Kolyvagin and Stark systems
method_transfers.method: represent rank-r arithmetic information by exterior-power system classes and use a higher-rank Kolyvagin-derivative formalism to constrain Selmer modules
shared_structure: the target obstruction is genuinely rank two rather than scalar
Selmer information is naturally encoded in cohomological modules
determinantal/exterior algebra is the correct language for simultaneous independent directions
required_assumptions: the p-adic representation and coefficient ring satisfy the system-theoretic hypotheses
the relevant higher-rank Euler/Stark/Kolyvagin system is nonzero in the target specialization
local conditions match the classical Selmer problem required for BSD
disanalogies: the formalism constructs and relates modules of systems but does not by itself derive target nontriviality from the complex condition L''(E,1) != 0
p-adic Selmer control alone does not supply the exact complex BSD leading coefficient
an exterior cohomology class need not automatically descend to two explicit independent rational points
method_transfers.repair_question: Can analytic rank two force target nontriviality of a rank-two Euler/Kolyvagin/Stark-system specialization without assuming a main conjecture equivalent in strength to the desired BSD conclusion?
source_anchors: Burns-Sano, On the Theory of Higher Rank Euler, Kolyvagin and Stark Systems, IMRN 2021(13), DOI 10.1093/imrn/rnz103

method_transfers.source_context: Chan-Ho Kim higher Gross-Zagier / Selmer-structure framework
method_transfers.method: separate Selmer-structure theorems from nontriviality questions and compare Heegner/Kato/bipartite system data through explicit reciprocity and main-conjecture localizations
shared_structure: the obstruction is not merely defining a rank-two formalism but proving the relevant system is nontrivial
root-number parity changes which geometric or quaternionic objects are available
arbitrary-rank Selmer structure can be studied before full analytic identification
required_assumptions: the working Galois-representation, reduction, and level hypotheses of the preprint
the stated nontriviality or localized main-conjecture inputs when invoked
careful separation of proved structure statements from conjectural or conditional analytic bridges
disanalogies: the preprint explicitly notes the number-field higher-rank analytic Gross-Zagier situation is substantially more difficult than rank at most one
its arbitrary-rank structural results do not constitute a generic proof that analytic rank two equals algebraic rank two
preprint status is not independent theorem authority for RAKL root promotion
method_transfers.repair_question: Which exact nontriviality statement in the rank-two even-sign setting has the strongest unconditional support, and what minimal additional theorem would connect it to L''(E,1) rather than to an assumed main conjecture?
source_anchors: Chan-Ho Kim, A higher Gross-Zagier formula and the structure of Selmer groups, arXiv:2203.12161, version dated 2026-03-22

explicit_disanalogies: the successful rank-one Heegner-point route cannot be copied by replacing 'one' with 'two' without proving independence and a determinant identity
nonzero Selmer classes do not automatically give rational points because Sha can absorb Selmer information
a p-adic main-conjecture or Iwasawa-theoretic equality is not the same object as the complex leading derivative in the Clay statement
a nonzero 2x2 regulator presupposes two independent global points and therefore cannot be used circularly to manufacture those points
special CM, twist-family, or local-prime results do not establish the generic elliptic-curve-over-Q rank-two bridge
unreviewed claims of a complete analytic-rank-two or full BSD proof are novelty-risk inputs only until independently validated

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A latent state with two independent degrees of freedom cannot be certified by a single scalar measurement direction; one seeks multiple independent probes whose information/Gram matrix has nonzero determinant.
common_abstraction: dimension-two hidden structure must be witnessed by two independent directions
a determinant tests whether nominally multiple witnesses collapse onto the same direction
existence of observations and identifiability of independent degrees of freedom are separate obligations
source_to_target_mapping: latent state directions -> independent Mordell-Weil generators
measurement/probe directions -> arithmetic cohomology or global point classes
information/Gram determinant -> exterior class or Neron-Tate regulator determinant
single observable -> classical rank-one Heegner-point witness
shared_constraints: duplicated or collinear witnesses do not certify dimension two
the determinant must be nonzero for structural reasons rather than numerical accident
the observation mechanism must actually couple to every target direction
disanalogies: BSD has no given linear measurement operator whose observability theory can be imported
analytic derivatives, Selmer classes, and rational points live in different categories and require theorems to relate them
a positive-definite information matrix in engineering does not imply a Neron-Tate height formula
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before searching for a rank-two formula, demand a determinant-level certificate with separately proved existence, independence, and analytic coupling; reject any route that only duplicates a rank-one witness.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: For any proposed rank-two bridge, prove that two arithmetic directions are genuinely independent, identify the exact determinant/exterior object, show why analytic rank two forces its nonvanishing, and exhibit a counterexample or failure mode when the two witnesses become dependent.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Structural analogy only; it motivates an independence test and cannot supply arithmetic or analytic theorem authority.

analogy_scan_notes: Scanned rank-one arithmetic bridges, higher-rank cohomological system formalisms, determinant/height structures, and cross-domain observability. Retained only the observability/determinant analogy because it exposes the exact independence failure that a naive two-copy rank-one strategy would miss.
